title: Lior and the Contact
premise: Odile Sterling, a veteran interpreter for a fractious peace delegation, has survived a decade of shifting protocols by staying small, precise, and unseen. When the delegation's safe house appears on a real estate listing — interior photos included, down to the coded documents on the kitchen table — Odile realizes someone inside their circle is selling them out, and that the 'accidental' gas leak planned for summit week is no accident at all. Partnering with Lior, the quiet security officer they've been carefully not falling in love with for three years, Odile must trace the listing to its source while deciding whether loyalty to duty or to each other matters more. In the end, Odile exposes the mole during the summit's opening session by deliberately mistranslating a single word, the attack is thwarted, and both choose exile over the institutions that used them — together.
about_author: Ada Brightwater is a former conference interpreter who spent years in rooms where one wrong word could end careers or start wars. She writes thrillers about the people who translate between power and consequence.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Silence
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Opening at a tense pre-summit briefing, Odile navigates a hostile negotiation session, establishing her precision and her careful distance from Lior, the security officer who watches her too closely. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism; the reader feels how much she edits herself.

chapters.title: For Sale: Furnished
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A junior staffer finds the safe house listed online with interior photos showing classified materials. Lior quietly begins an internal sweep while concealing the breach from superiors who might burn the whole team. Emotional beat: creeping dread; the safe world is revealed as a stage set.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flashback interwoven with present: how Odile learned that protocols change whenever convenient, and how she once lost a colleague to a 'corrected' translation. She recognizes the listing's staging style — it mirrors her own habits. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing; identity shaken.

chapters.title: The Third Chair
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior narrows suspects to three insiders and requests Odile's help reading linguistic tells in leaked documents. Working through the night, the professional distance finally cracks into honesty. Emotional beat: reluctant intimacy; two guarded people discovering they've been guarding the same wound.

chapters.title: What the Listing Didn't Show
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The team relocates, but Odile notices the photos omit one room — the listening room — meaning the seller wanted them looking there, not at the real target. First hint the attack aims at the summit venue itself. Emotional beat: sharp clarity; fear transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Duty Is a Kind of Debt
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior's handler orders him to stand down and let the intelligence services handle it — an order that smells like containment of a scandal rather than prevention. Torn, he chooses Odile's plan over protocol. Emotional beat: love against duty made explicit; betrayal by institution.

chapters.title: Mistranslation as a Weapon
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile and Lior identify the mole via a phrase pattern only an interpreter would catch — the mole is another linguist, someone Odile trained. They set a trap using a false document seeded into the next session. Emotional beat: bitter recognition; the mentor seeing her own methods turned against her.

chapters.title: The Quiet Before
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Summit eve. The trap half-works: the mole panics but accelerates the timeline, moving the attack to the opening session. Odile and Lior share a fragile, almost-confessed moment knowing tomorrow may end everything. Emotional beat: tenderness under countdown pressure.

chapters.title: One Word Wrong on Purpose
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, climax. During the opening session, Odile mistranslates a single critical term to force the mole's handler to abort, exposing the plot publicly while Lior intercepts the device crew backstage. Chaos, near-failure, and the mole's arrest. Emotional beat: white-knuckle courage; Odile weaponizes the very skill that erased her.

chapters.title: Exits
chapters.summary: Dual POV resolution. Both are quietly pushed out — too visible now, too compromised. Instead of fighting for reinstatement, they walk away together, trading the institution for something chosen rather than assigned. Final image: a new city, a new language neither speaks yet. Emotional beat: found family realized; freedom as the reward for truth.
